videos.script: Lesson six made identities. This lesson says what they may do. {{doc}} A policy is a short JSON document. Each statement has an effect, allow or deny. It names actions, such as reading an object, and resources, such as one bucket. {{kinds}} Policies come in three kinds. AWS writes some, and edits them on its own schedule. You write others, and keep up to five versions of each. And some are written straight into one user, and leave with that user. {{moto}} This is also the lesson where moto starts to judge. Until now it said yes to everything. You restart it with a count of three. Three requests go through unchecked, and they make an administrator. After that, every request is signed and judged. {{bia}} Then bia, the shop's developer, gets a policy of her own. She reads the assets bucket. She is refused the backups, and the list of users. {{refusal}} The refusals are real, and each service words them its own way. By the end, you can write a policy, choose its kind, and watch it decide. {{end}}
